content.rendered:
Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Two verbs. Both active. Both present tense. Both belonging to the believer. Both anchored in the finished work of Christ.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, July 21, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.”
James 4:7 (NIV)

Today’s Message

James writes with the practical directness of the Lord’s brother who has watched Him lead crowds through fields and streets in Galilee. His letters do not spend long paragraphs building theological arguments. They lay down commands and expect action. James 4:7 is one of the shortest, sharpest, and most consequential sentences in his entire letter. Submit to God. Resist the devil. He will flee.

The order matters. Submission comes first. Before the believer raises a voice against the enemy, they yield to the Father. This is the difference between the New Testament pattern of spiritual authority and every self-help version of the same idea. The believer’s authority is not intrinsic to them. It is exercised under the authority of God. Submission to God is what makes resistance to the devil effective. The believer who resists without first submitting is trying to fight from their own resources. That does not work. The believer who has yielded to the Father, on the other hand, resists from a position that carries heaven’s weight.

The Greek verb for “resist” is antistēte. It means to stand against, to withstand, to refuse to yield ground. It is a military term. Picture a soldier bracing at a fixed position, refusing to be moved. James is not telling the believer to run at the enemy. He is telling the believer to stand in the place Christ has already given them, refuse to yield an inch, and speak the truth in the name of Jesus. The enemy is the one who is moving, not the believer.

And James makes an extraordinary promise about what happens when the believer resists. The devil will flee. The Greek verb is pheuxetai. It means to run away, to escape, to make a hasty departure. It is the same verb used in the Gospels to describe demons fleeing from Jesus. James is drawing a straight line. The devil who fled from Jesus in the wilderness will flee from the believer who resists in Jesus’ name. Same enemy. Same result. The cross has stripped him of his authority. His only tactic left is deception. When the believer stops agreeing with the deception and stands on the finished work of Christ, the enemy runs.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the truth this morning is practical. The enemy is not omnipotent. He is defeated. His only remaining strategy is to bluff. When you submit to God and resist him in the name of Jesus, the bluff collapses. He flees. Not because you are strong. Because Christ is Lord and you are standing on the ground Christ has already secured. Practise that today. Submit. Resist. Watch him go.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I have submitted my life to You. I yield to Your will, Your wisdom, Your Word today. From that submitted position, I resist the devil in the name of Jesus. I refuse to yield ground on any front. I refuse to agree with his deception. I refuse to accept his accusations. I refuse to entertain his suggestions. He must flee, because You have declared it. Christ has already defeated him at the cross. I walk in that victory today, submitted to You, resistant to him, and confident in the ground Jesus has secured. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am submitted to God. I resist the devil in the name of Jesus. He must flee. The cross has stripped him of his authority. I walk on ground Christ has already secured.
